messages:
alex: FYI customer reported intermittent 400s on /v1/embeddings, says vectors look fine but server complains about shape.

maria: which customer? any example payloads or client code? :thinking:

alex: Acme (SRE). They sent a repro from a web client using fetch. Pasted below. They say sometimes it works, sometimes returns 400.

alex: ```js
// client code they shared
const payload = JSON.stringify({ input: JSON.stringify([0.12, 0.03, ...]) });
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}`, "Content-Type": 'application/json' },
  body: payload
})
```

devon: ohhh double-stringify. they're turning the vector into a string then wrapping in JSON again. that would produce a string field instead of an array. server expects an array of floats or list of arrays.

embed-ops-bot: Log from infra @ 3048881800: "400 invalid_embedding_shape: expected list of floats (dim=1536) or list of lists, got string at path input[0]"

maria: that explains the 400. Why intermittent?

alex: customer says they batch some requests client-side; some code paths produce raw arrays, others do JSON.stringify first (older helper). so mixed payload forms hit the API. when mixed in a single batch we sometimes see a 400 for the whole request.

devon: repro steps I ran locally: 1) send single request with input as string -> 400 with same message. 2) send single request with input as array -> 200. 3) send batch where one item is string and another is array -> 400 for entire request (server rejects).

devon: paste of the failing HTTP body I sent (content-type application/json):
```json
{ "input": ["[0.12,0.03,...]", [0.11,0.02,...]] }
```

maria: thanks. actionable items: 1) tell customer to stop double-stringifying, change helper to avoid JSON.stringify on the inner vector. 2) recommend a quick client-side validation before send: typeof item === 'string' && try JSON.parse to coerce, or better ensure arrays only. 3) we'll add a clearer error message on our side suggesting "found string at input[i] — did you JSON.stringify vectors?" in next patch.

alex: suggested reply to customer: include minimal repro, show the two variants and the fix. also include cURL examples for correct vs incorrect.

maria: I'll draft the reply. quick snippet for them: correct body:```json
{ "input": [[0.12,0.03,...]] }
``` incorrect (what they were sending):```json
{ "input": ["[0.12,0.03,...]"] }
```

maria: and JS fix:```js
// bad
const item = JSON.stringify(vec); // <- remove this
// good
const item = vec; // pass array directly
fetch(..., { body: JSON.stringify({ input: [item] }) })
```

alex: customer also reported some 429 spikes earlier — likely unrelated but we should flag if they batch huge numbers. i asked for their batch sizes.

devon: +1 on adding validation. also note Content-Type mismatches can cause issues: if someone sets text/plain they sometimes send NDJSON lines; server supports JSON array only in this endpoint (we have separate ndjson ingestion for streaming). I'll add a short note to docs.

maria: I'll send patch: update support guide with common client mistakes (double-stringify, text/plain, mixing single/batch shapes). will follow up with customer message and close once they confirm fix. :white_check_mark:

alex: thanks — cc @devops if we want to improve error text in next runtime release.
